_comment: Cloud Monitoring alert policies. GitLab #39 Stage 2.
WHY OUT-OF-BAND. Every check inside the nightly only runs when the nightly runs. The
failure that cost six days of stale data (2026-08-03 to 08-09) was the nightly NOT
RUNNING AT ALL - a cron silently dropped by a platform migration. No in-pipeline test can
ever see that.
WHY THESE MEASURE DATA AGE AND NOT JOB SUCCESS. The first design alerted on the absence
of a successful fdp-nightly execution. It worked, but job success is a PROXY: a pipeline
that 'succeeds' nightly while writing nothing is stale and would never have tripped it.
It also ran into a hard platform cap - conditionAbsent rejects durations over 23h30m and
MQL absent_for over 1d1h, while for a DAILY job anything at or below 24h fires before
every run - leaving 25h as a ceiling rather than a choice. The CPO chose to measure the
real signal instead: scripts/check_raw_freshness.py reads each raw table's last-modified
time and exits non-zero when it is past the error_after already declared in sources.yml.
Running that sentinel HOURLY also dissolves the cap: absence detection on an hourly job
needs a 3h window, far inside the limit.
Applied by the commands in deploy/nightly/README.md, which strip every key starting with
`_` (the API rejects unknown fields) and inject the notification channel id read back from
the API rather than hardcoded.

policies.displayName: fdp raw data is STALE or uncheckable
_comment: THE IMPORTANT ONE. Fires when scripts/check_raw_freshness.py exits NON-ZERO.
⚠ IT CANNOT DISTINGUISH exit 1 (a table is genuinely past error_after) from exit 2
(the sentinel could not check - unreadable thresholds, BigQuery unreachable, a table
that will not answer). Cloud Run's completed_execution_count metric carries only
succeeded/failed, not the process exit code, so both surface identically. An earlier
draft of this documentation asserted 'users are affected', which is not established on
an exit 2; a reviewer caught it. The title and text now cover both, and the log says
which one it was in its first line.
Both are worth waking up for, which is why they share a policy rather than being
separated with a log-based metric: stale data means users see yesterday's football,
and a sentinel that cannot check means we have lost the ability to tell.
Thresholds are NOT here. They live in sources.yml (warn 30h / error 54h on 8 of the
11 sources; 3 deliberately have none because they refresh rarely). One definition, so
there is nothing to drift.

documentation.content:
The freshness sentinel exited non-zero. That is EITHER stale data OR an inability to check - the alert cannot tell which, so read the log first.

  exit 1 = a raw table is past its `error_after` (see `dbt_project/models/1_staging/api_football/sources.yml`). Users are affected: Matchday Pilot serves fixtures, so stale raw means yesterday's football.
  exit 2 = the sentinel could NOT check (unreadable thresholds, BigQuery unreachable, a table that will not answer). The data may be fine; we have lost the ability to say so.

Cloud Run's execution metric carries only succeeded/failed, not the exit code, which is why one policy covers both. The sentinel's log states which, and names the table and its age:
  gcloud run jobs executions list --job fdp-freshness --region europe-west1 --limit 5
  gcloud logging read 'resource.type="cloud_run_job" AND resource.labels.job_name="fdp-freshness"' --limit 30 --order=desc

If it is exit 1, ask why the nightly is not landing data:
  gcloud run jobs executions list --job fdp-nightly --region europe-west1 --limit 5
  gcloud scheduler jobs describe fdp-nightly --location europe-west1

Runbook: deploy/nightly/README.md

conditionThreshold.filter: resource.type = "cloud_run_job" AND resource.labels.job_name = "fdp-freshness" AND metric.type = "run.googleapis.com/job/completed_execution_count" AND metric.labels.result = "failed"

_comment: WATCHES THE WATCHER. The sentinel is the only thing that can see a stopped pipeline,
so a sentinel that stops takes the visibility with it and everything looks fine.
3h of absence on an HOURLY job: two missed runs plus slack. This is the shape the
original design could not use - conditionAbsent caps at 23h30m, which is useless for
a DAILY signal but generous for an hourly one. Running the check often is what makes
cheap absence detection possible.
The regress stops here deliberately: nothing watches Cloud Scheduler and Cloud
Monitoring themselves. They are managed services with their own status surface, and a
third monitor is where this stops being proportionate.

documentation.content:
The freshness sentinel (`fdp-freshness`) has not run successfully in 3 hours. It is scheduled hourly.

This does NOT mean the data is stale. It means we can no longer TELL whether it is - which is the same blind spot that let six days of stale data pass unnoticed in August 2026.

CHECK:
  gcloud run jobs executions list --job fdp-freshness --region europe-west1 --limit 5
  gcloud scheduler jobs describe fdp-freshness --location europe-west1

Meanwhile, check freshness by hand - it is a free metadata read:
  bq show --format=prettyjson football-data-pipeline-gcp:raw.RAW_APIF_FIXTURES_NEXT

Exit code 2 from the sentinel means 'could not check' (unreadable thresholds, BigQuery unreachable, a table that will not answer) and is deliberately not 0 - a sentinel that cannot check must never look healthy.

Runbook: deploy/nightly/README.md

conditionAbsent.filter: resource.type = "cloud_run_job" AND resource.labels.job_name = "fdp-freshness" AND metric.type = "run.googleapis.com/job/completed_execution_count" AND metric.labels.result = "succeeded"

_comment: Kept from the first design and still worth having: it names the CAUSE (the nightly
broke) hours before the effect (data crosses error_after) would show up. Not a
substitute for the staleness policy - a nightly can fail without the data being stale
yet, and data can go stale without the nightly ever failing.

documentation.content:
A football-data-pipeline nightly execution FAILED.

The data is not necessarily stale YET - `error_after` is 54h on most sources, so there is room for a retry tonight. This is the early warning; `fdp raw data is STALE or uncheckable` is the one that fires when users may actually be affected (exit 1) or when we have lost the ability to tell (exit 2).

  gcloud run jobs executions list --job fdp-nightly --region europe-west1 --limit 5
  gcloud logging read 'resource.type="cloud_run_job" AND resource.labels.job_name="fdp-nightly"' --limit 50 --order=desc

No retry happens automatically: the job is deployed with --max-retries 0 because the BigQuery ingest lock holds a lease and an immediate retry would be refused. Recovery is the next scheduled run.

Runbook: deploy/nightly/README.md

conditionThreshold.filter: resource.type = "cloud_run_job" AND resource.labels.job_name = "fdp-nightly" AND metric.type = "run.googleapis.com/job/completed_execution_count" AND metric.labels.result = "failed"
